summary: Validated the density-suggestion Apply fix for AI-Agent-generated slides (html-type elements). Direct GeneratedPanel UI testing was not feasible (step=6 only renders after a full generation flow, no URL-based shortcut). Instead, validated the IDENTICAL onApply pattern via the Editor's SlideProperties flow on a real AI-Agent generated project (projectId 83dffbd3-5aee-4140-b81c-f0395c061a6b, slide 2 with 3x html-type elements). Flow worked end-to-end: density dialog opened, text content was correctly extracted from html-type elements, 3 LLM suggestions rendered with transformedText/transformedBullets, clicking Aplicar collapsed the 5 original elements (Html 1/2, Image 3, Html 4, Text 5) into 2 (single Html with new bullets + Image preserved). Original prose was REPLACED, not appended. GeneratedPanel.jsx onApply (lines 414-525) is a direct mirror of this verified logic — same TEXTUAL_TYPES=['text','html','paragraph','title','heading'], same htmlContent builder, same drop-leftovers semantics, same plainText/htmlContent dual write for html-type elements.

issues: After density Aplicar, the replaced html element keeps its original x/y/width/height — with much shorter bullet content, the canvas looks mostly empty in the top-left while the image stays at its original right-side coordinates. Cosmetic only; not part of this fix's scope but worth tracking.

action_items: Optional (not part of this P0 fix): when applying a density suggestion to a html-type element, consider recalculating element height (or auto-shrinking width) so the new shorter content does not leave an empty visual gap on the canvas. Same minor issue would surface in GeneratedPanel too.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix logic in GeneratedPanel.jsx lines 414-525 is correct and mirrors the working SlideProperties.jsx pattern: (a) text-collector at line 421 includes 'html', (b) TEXTUAL_TYPES at line 451 includes 'html', (c) line 493 writes htmlContent when target.type==='html' (preventing the orphan-append bug), (d) lines 496-497 drop other textual elements so the new prose does not compete with leftovers.

Minor: line 493 ternary `isHtmlType || tgtEl.htmlContent ? htmlContent : undefined` — passing undefined into a spread will set the property to undefined explicitly rather than leaving it absent. Harmless because renderers fall back to content, but a delete + conditional spread would be slightly cleaner.

Both the Editor (SlideProperties) and Agent (GeneratedPanel) onApply handlers duplicate ~80 lines of identical logic — candidate for extraction into a shared hook/util (e.g. useApplyDensitySuggestion(slideId, projectId)). Not a blocker.
seed_data_creation: None. Used existing session 369d26ec-7b3f-4f16-ba04-05c2fba54cc6 / project 83dffbd3-5aee-4140-b81c-f0395c061a6b (Combate à fraude nas empresas.docx, step=generated, 3 html elements on slide 2).
context_for_next_testing_agent: To exercise GeneratedPanel.jsx directly the user must traverse the full /agent flow (mode=create → upload → analyze → storyboard → media → generate) which is slow and expensive. There is no ?editMedia query-param shortcut to step 6: ?editMedia lands on step 5 (MediaConfig). The Editor's SlideProperties.jsx is functionally identical for the density-apply path and is the recommended proxy test target. To replicate this run: login admin@scormify.com/admin123 → open /editor/83dffbd3-5aee-4140-b81c-f0395c061a6b → click slide 2 → click 'Analisar densidade e sugerir melhorias' in the Properties panel → wait ~10s for LLM → click any 'Aplicar'. Note also a stale-cache concern: many MongoDB agent_sessions have step='generated' with valid projectId — those projects can be loaded via /editor/{projectId} as a fast way to test against real html-type AI-generated slides.
rca of the issue:
Original bug: GeneratedPanel.onApply searched elements with `type === 'text'` only. AI-Agent-generated slides use `type === 'html'` (rich content containers with both .content AND .htmlContent), so the lookup returned [], the else branch fired and pushed a brand-new text element with the suggestion at (80,80) — leaving the original html element intact behind it, hence 'nothing visible changed + orphan appended'. The fix widens the lookup to TEXTUAL_TYPES (['text','html','paragraph','title','heading']), and when the target is html-type writes BOTH .content (plain text) and .htmlContent (proper

/

  • markup). Mitigation verified in mirrored Editor flow; the canvas correctly drops 4 of 5 elements and replaces the surviving html element's content with the new bullet markup.
